questions.q: The binary equivalent of decimal 156 is:
Which shortcut selects the **entire row** containing the active cell?
questions.solution: **Shift+Space = row**, Ctrl+Space = column.

questions.q: The default extension of a Word 2007 or later document is —
questions.solution: **.docx** is the Office Open XML default from Word 2007 onwards; .doc is the 97-2003 file.

questions.q: Which view prints one slide at the top with the speaker notes below it?
questions.solution: **Notes Page** lays out the slide above its notes — designed for the presenter's printout.

questions.q:
Read the paragraph and choose the option that best expresses its main idea.

Companies that moved fully remote cut office costs sharply, and employees saved hours of commuting each week. But managers report that new joiners learn slower without senior colleagues nearby, and several firms have quietly started mentor-buddy programmes.
options: Remote work has failed because new employees cannot learn.
Remote work saves money and time but slows the training of new staff.
Mentor-buddy programmes are the future of corporate HR.
Office rents are falling across big cities.
questions.solution: The paragraph gives two gains (costs, commute) and one cost (slow training for new joiners), ending on the mentor fix. Option 2 covers all of it at the same scope. Option 1 overstates ("has failed"), option 3 promotes a detail into the main idea, option 4 introduces rent markets.

questions.q: What does the author mean by describing the deeper cost of gig work as 'invisible'?
options: Platforms hide their profits from tax authorities
The loss of financial stability undermines workers' ability to plan, borrow and save, though no ledger records it
Customers do not see the workers who deliver to them
The cost of running the app is unknown to investors
questions.solution: The sentence itself defines the term: 'a workforce that cannot plan a month ahead also cannot borrow, train or save with confidence' — a damage to financial planning that appears in no account book, hence invisible. (b) captures this. (a) and (d) move to taxes and investors, topics the passage never raises; (c) is literal 'seeing', exactly the misreading the word invites.
questions.shortcut: When a passage defines its own metaphor in the next clause, the answer is inside that clause — match it, not the literal image.
questions.passage:
The app has changed not only how we order food but what it means to have a job. Across the world, millions now earn through platforms that assign work task by task: a ride, a delivery, a design project. Companies celebrate this flexibility, and for some workers it is real — a student can drive between lectures, a parent can log off when the school day ends. Yet the same arrangement shifts nearly every risk of doing business onto the individual. The platform owns the technology, sets the price and directs the customer to the worker; the worker owns the vehicle, the fuel, the insurance and the idle hours between jobs.

Because a gig worker is classified as an independent partner rather than an employee, she generally falls outside labour laws written for factories and offices. No minimum wage applies to hours spent waiting for a request, no paid leave cushions an illness, and contributions to a pension depend entirely on what the worker chooses, or can afford, to set aside. Several countries are now experimenting with a middle category that would grant platform workers some protections without ending flexible scheduling.

Economists warn that the deeper cost may be invisible: a workforce that cannot plan a month ahead also cannot borrow, train or save with confidence. If algorithms increasingly decide who works and for how much, the question is not whether such work will disappear — it will grow — but whether the rules governing it will grow with it. Societies have rewritten labour law before, when work moved from fields to factories; the same imagination can be applied now.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.  He is the ___ boy in the class.
questions.solution: 'The ... in the class' signals a superlative → **tallest**.

questions.q: Which of the following questions can be answered from the passage?
options: How much does it cost to rent one beehive?
Why do some villages spray pesticides only in the evening?
Which apple variety needs the most bees?
In which year did wild bees start declining?
questions.solution: The passage says villages spray 'only in the evening, when bees are resting' — that answers the 'why'. It calls renting 'costly' but gives no figure, names no apple variety, and gives no year.
questions.shortcut: 'Costly' is not a cost figure — questions asking 'how much' need a number in the passage.
questions.passage:
Farmers in parts of Himachal Pradesh have begun renting beehives each spring. They place the boxes among their apple trees for a few weeks and return them after the flowers fade. The reason is simple: the wild bees that once did this work free of charge have become scarce.

Scientists point to several causes. Heavy use of pesticides kills bees directly, and orchards planted with a single crop leave few wild flowers to feed them once the fruit blossom is over. Warmer winters also disturb the match between flowering time and the insects' active season.

Renting hives helps, but it is costly, and the hired bees do not reach every orchard. Some villages have tried a cheaper approach: they leave strips of wild flowers along field edges and spray only in the evening, when bees are resting. Early results suggest that such steps bring wild pollinators back within a few seasons. The lesson is that nature's free services are free only as long as we protect them.

questions.q: Which planet has the largest moon of the solar system, Ganymede?
questions.solution: **Ganymede**, a moon of **Jupiter**, is the largest natural satellite in the solar system — bigger than Mercury. Saturn's largest moon is Titan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bank Rate is kept equal to the MSF rate.
2. The dormant reverse repo rate of 3.35% is currently the operative floor of the liquidity corridor.
3. The SDF allows banks to park funds with the RBI without providing collateral.

Which of the statements are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct — the Bank Rate moves with the MSF. Statement 3 is correct — the SDF needs no collateral. Statement 2 is wrong: since **April 2022 the SDF, not the dormant reverse repo (3.35%), is the operative floor**.
questions.shortcut: Reverse repo is dormant; the SDF is the working floor.

questions.q: Tilak started the public **Ganapati festival** in 1893 primarily to —
options: Build a mass base against British rule
questions.solution: The **Ganapati (1893)** and **Shivaji (1895)** festivals gave Tilak a legal platform to gather and mobilise the masses.
questions.shortcut: Festivals = political mobilisation under a religious cover.

questions.q: An economy shows **rising prices along with falling output and rising unemployment**. This is —
questions.solution: **Stagflation** = stagnation (weak growth, job losses) plus inflation — the classic outcome of a severe cost-push shock, as in the 1970s oil crises.

questions.q: In how many ways can 8 people be divided into two teams of 4 each?
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{8!}{4!\,4!} = 70$ pairs of named teams.
The two teams are interchangeable: $70 \div 2 = 35$.
questions.shortcut: 70 counts 'Team A vs Team B' twice — equal groups divide by 2!.

questions.q: Find the sum $1 \times 2 + 2 \times 4 + 3 \times 8 + 4 \times 16 + 5 \times 32 + 6 \times 64$.
questions.solution:
Terms: 2, 8, 24, 64, 160, 384.
Shift-and-subtract with $r = 2$ (or add directly): $S = 642$.

questions.q: Two rods measure 12 m 60 cm and 7 m 20 cm. They are cut into pieces of equal length, the length being the greatest possible. Find the length of a piece and the total number of pieces.
questions.solution:
In centimetres: 1260 and 720. Greatest length $= \gcd(1260, 720) = 180$ cm $= 1$ m 80 cm.
Total pieces $= \frac{1260 + 720}{180} = \frac{1980}{180} = 11$ (7 from the long rod + 4 from the short one).
questions.shortcut: 90 cm and 60 cm also measure both rods exactly, but the question wants the greatest length.

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{4x+1}{x-4}$, then $f^{-1}(5)$ equals:
questions.solution:
Here $a = 4$ and the bottom constant is $-4 = -a$, so $f$ is self-inverse.
$f^{-1}(5) = f(5) = \dfrac{21}{1} = 21$.
Check: $f(21) = \dfrac{85}{17} = 5$. ✓
questions.shortcut: Self-inverse: bottom constant $=-$ top coefficient of $x$.

questions.q: In a housing society of **150 families, 90 have a car, 70 have a two-wheeler and 40 have both**. How many families have **neither**?
questions.solution: At least one = 90 + 70 − 40 = 120. Neither = 150 − 120 = **30**. 70 comes from 150 − (50 + 30), which forgets the 40 families who have both.

questions.q: In a certain code, **PENCIL** is written as **LFODJP**. How is **MARKET** written in that code?
questions.solution: PENCIL → LFODJP: the first and last letters are interchanged (P…L → L…P) and the middle letters ENCI each move +1 → FODJ. MARKET: T…M at the ends, middle ARKE +1 → BSLF → **TBSLFM**.
questions.shortcut: Two jobs: swap the ends, shift the middle by the same +1.

questions.q: Select the pair that fills both blanks: **? : Kitten :: Dog : ?**
questions.solution: Both sides must read **adult : young**. Cat : Kitten ✓ and Dog : Puppy ✓. Kennel is a home and bark a sound, so those options break the link.
